item.title: “Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the defilement of beings. Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the purification of beings.” “But,…
item.description:
“Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the defilement of beings. Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the purification of beings.” “But, venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition for the defilement of beings?” “Mahāli, if form were exclusively suffering, immersed in suffering, accompanied by suffering, not accompanied by happiness, beings would not become lustful for form. But because form is happiness, Mahāli, immersed in happiness, accompanied by happiness, not accompanied by suffering, beings become lustful for form. Through lust, they are bound; through being bound, they are defiled. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the defilement of beings. Such being the cause, such being the condition, beings are defiled.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.60

item.title: - What hangs up the world? What envelops the world? What closes in the world? Upon what does the world stand? - Craving hangs up…
item.description:
- What hangs up the world?
What envelops the world?
What closes in the world?
Upon what does the world stand?
- Craving hangs up the world,
Aging envelops the world,
Death closes in the world,
Upon suffering the world stands.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.67

item.title: - “Venerable Sāriputta, what things should a virtuous monk attend to wisely?” - “Venerable Koṭṭhika, a virtuous monk should attend wisely to the five aggregates…
item.description:
- “Venerable Sāriputta, what things should a virtuous monk attend to wisely?” - “Venerable Koṭṭhika, a virtuous monk should attend wisely to the five aggregates of clinging as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease, as a boil, as a dart, as misery, as an affliction, as alien, as disintegrating, as empty, as not-self. What five? The form aggregate of clinging, the feeling aggregate of clinging, the perception aggregate of clinging, the formation aggregate of clinging, the consciousness aggregate of clinging. Venerable Koṭṭhika, a virtuous monk should attend wisely to these five aggregates of clinging as impermanent … as not-self.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.122
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, an untaught ordinary person does not know as it actually is the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard…
item.description:
“Monks, an untaught ordinary person does not know as it actually is the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard to form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. Monks, a well-taught noble disciple knows as it actually is the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard to form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.74
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Venerable sir, how does future rebirth occur?” “Venerable sir, when beings are shrouded by ignorance and bound by craving, delighting here and there, thus future…
item.description:
“Venerable sir, how does future rebirth occur?” “Venerable sir, when beings are shrouded by ignorance and bound by craving, delighting here and there, thus future rebirth occurs.” “Venerable sir, how does future rebirth not occur?” “Venerable sir, when ignorance is abandoned, knowledge arises, and craving is destroyed, thus future rebirth does not occur.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 43 – Mahāvedallasutta

item.title: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, king fights with king, noble warrior…
item.description:
“Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, king fights with king, noble warrior fights with noble warrior, brahmin fights with brahmin, householder fights with householder, mother fights with child, child fights with mother, father fights with child, child fights with father, brother fights with brother, brother fights with sister, sister fights with brother, friend fights with friend. Having engaged in quarrels, disputes, and battles, they attack one another with fists, with stones, with sticks, with swords. There they meet death or deadly suffering. Monks, such is the peril of sensuality, a mass of suffering visible here and now, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis – simply because of sensuality.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 13 – Mahādukkhakkhandhasutta

item.title: Standing to one side, the deity Uttara recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One: Life is swept along, Short is the lifespan…
item.description:
Standing to one side, the deity Uttara recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
Life is swept along,
Short is the lifespan —
To old age we are led,
There is no stopping place.
Seeing this danger in death,
Do meritorious deeds
That bring true happiness.

Life is swept along,
Short is the lifespan —
To old age we are led,
There is no stopping place.
Seeing this danger in death,
Seeking peace, abandon worldly hopes.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.19
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Cunda, just as all unwholesome states tend downward and all wholesome states tend upward. So too, Cunda: the harmless person is higher than the harmful…
item.description:
“Cunda, just as all unwholesome states tend downward and all wholesome states tend upward. So too, Cunda: the harmless person is higher than the harmful person; the person who abstains from killing is higher than the killer; the person who abstains from taking what is not given is higher than the taker of what is not given; the person unsmeared by the world, not clinging to personal views, of easy disposition and equanimity, is higher than the person smeared by the world, clinging to personal views, of difficult disposition and lacking equanimity.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 8 – Sallekhasutta

item.title: Then the Blessed One gave progressive instruction to the brahmin Pokkharasādi, namely: talk on giving, talk on virtue, talk on the heavens; he explained the…
item.description:
Then the Blessed One gave progressive instruction to the brahmin Pokkharasādi, namely: talk on giving, talk on virtue, talk on the heavens; he explained the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that the brahmin Pokkharasādi’s mind was ready, pliant, free from hindrances, uplifted, and confident, he then taught the Dhamma that the Buddhas have realized, namely: suffering, origin, cessation, and path. Just as a clean cloth, freed from black stains, would properly absorb dye, so too, right there in that seat, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in the brahmin Pokkharasādi: ‘Whatever is subject to origination is all subject to cessation.’

From: Dīgha Nikāya 3 – Ambaṭṭhasutta

item.title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, that leads to such great benefit as heedfulness. Heedfulness, monks, leads to great benefit.”
item.description:
“I do not see any other thing, monks, that leads to such great benefit as heedfulness. Heedfulness, monks, leads to great benefit.”
